notes: The run did the mechanics right (branch, exclusions, split commits, tests before push, staleness called out with the exact false claims, CI honesty) and the body's numbers all trace to BENCHMARKS.md; the two failures are both prose shape, and they are real: the Why lead is one 52-word sentence that tries to be the whole argument. Eval critique: assertion 14 (numbers present) would also pass a body that pastes the BENCHMARKS table without interpreting it, so it checks presence, not that the trade-off is framed as a cost; assertion 16's 'plain sentences' is not machine-checkable and the 'one sentence' part duplicates what prose-lint's long-lead rule already catches, so the two assertions move together. Nothing checks that the fixture's pre-existing commit b8d850a was left alone (it was) or that the agent did not amend/force-push, which is the most expensive failure mode for an existing-PR scenario and is cheap to assert via origin's reflog or the unchanged SHA. The agent's flagged unverified claims ('No new dependencies', 'callers still check allow() before send()') are the kind of honesty the eval could reward but no assertion touches.
